manual.why_not_upstream: no package can be built from the upstream manual. It declares `slid(o, dir)`; a push moves the box and carries the pusher, so a two-argument slide leaves half its own effect unnamed and there is nothing to tell a reader the event does. It also leaves `dir` a free name, which the executable and proof backends refuse. The shipped file is that manual with the v0.3 repairs (X-1, X-5), every rule bound over a declared `domain direction`.

playbook.why_absent: a0-spike ships no playbook file. This package is tier `manual` because that is what the arm produced, not because a tier was withheld.
